# Ellen West

## Overview

- **Age:** Ten years older than her sister Rosemary West  <sub>[v5 c13 P25](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0025)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v5 c22 P0](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0000)</sub>

## Appearance

Ellen is a tall, massive, and handsome woman with a stately figure. She has black hair, thick black eyebrows, and clear, slaty blue eyes resembling gulf water in a north wind. She possesses a rather stern, forbidding look.

_Sources: [v5 c22 P8](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0008), [v5 c13 P25](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0025)_

## Personality

Despite a stern appearance, Ellen is jolly, splendidly sincere, and possesses a strong sense of humor and a hearty, gurgling laugh. She has a deep, mellow, pleasant voice with a masculine quality and an intellectual grasp of politics and world events. She strongly dislikes being alone, often talking aloud to avoid solitude, and enjoys spirited, rousing arguments with articulate men.

_Sources: [v5 c22 P3](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0003), [v5 c21 P8](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0008), [v5 c21 P10](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0010), [v5 c13 P25](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0025)_

## History

Ellen West resided with her younger sister Rosemary in their homestead on the hill near Glen St. Mary. Years earlier, she had been courted by Norman Douglas before his sudden marriage, though she eventually came to regard him almost as a stranger. When the Glen minister, John Meredith, visited their house to borrow a book, Ellen engaged him in a lively conversation about global politics and the potential threat of the German Kaiser. Although she enjoyed Mr. Meredith's company and considered him a fine prospective brother-in-law, she held Rosemary to a past promise that prevented her sister from accepting his marriage proposal. At a silver wedding party hosted by the Pollocks, Ellen re-encountered Norman Douglas and successfully bested him in a spirited argument. Upon returning home late that night, she found Rosemary distressed over having refused Mr. Meredith. Later, Norman Douglas directly confronted Rosemary in Rainbow Valley, persuading her to release Ellen from their old vow so that Ellen and Norman could marry.

_Sources: [v5 c13 P19](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0019), [v5 c13 P24](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0024), [v5 c13 P25](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0025), [v5 c13 P27](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0027), [v5 c13 P29](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0029), [v5 c21 P11](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0011), [v5 c21 P12](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0012), [v5 c22 P0](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0000), [v5 c22 P1](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0001), [v5 c22 P3](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0003), [v5 c22 P5](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0005), [v5 c22 P9](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0009), [v5 c32 P12](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0012)_
